newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes ease, buyers seen fading.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes ease, buyers seen fading.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices eased in line with lower WTI/Cushing values Thursday, with discussion expected to dry up following yesterday's sale of full Alaskan crude cargo, traders said.
"Buyers will wait a while. There's no hurry to buy April," one trader said.
BP sold 300,000 barrels of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude to Chevron for April delivery at $1.00 under April WTI.
Traders said Chevron might need ANS for its Hawaii refinery, which needs supply commited early because of delivery complications.
The deal tightened the ANS differential from its previous level of minus $1.10, the price of a cargo sold in mid-February.
ANS outright prices fell to $19.85/20.05 a barrel, in line with WTI market caught in the downdraught of falling sour grades in the U.S. Gulf.
Line 63 prices stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05. One trader said the posting plus market, with gravity adjustments, stood at a slight premium to ANS.
"(Chevron) is willing to buy at $1.00 (under WTI) because its cheaper than a Buena Vista," posting basis, a trader said.
He said Chevron might lower its California Buena Vista postings as a result.
Kern River heavy crude stayed steady after falling Monday, with prices talked 13.84/14.04 a barrel, traders said.
